conclusion.statement: dsh-context@0.59.0 (artifact sha256 cd72cae6f1073ea2391389e0c7203050f970b8fb818063770b76fb145277d96d) was exercised on Node 22 and Node 24 across the plugin's evidenced Web plane and the two declared DSH baselines. Launch exited 0 with 8 executed cells, 0 failed tasks, 4 native + 4 surface cells, 0 adapter cells. Web plane on the current baseline dsh 0.1.7-rc.2 passed every stage (runtime, artifact, profile, install, registration, host, surface, interaction, shutdown) on BOTH Node 22 and Node 24: the Web host mounted and the declared plugin client entry was published, fetched, and materialized. Native load cells on 0.1.7-rc.2 returned 'unknown' on both majors because dependency coverage is incomplete (4 missing Node peers, 0 indeterminate, 0 version facts, 0 unresolved edges) — the exact artifact installed and loaded, and this is explicitly not a demonstrated runtime failure. Native cells on the declared baseline dsh 0.1.5-rc.1 were 'compatible' on both majors (installed, registered, loaded, direct Node peer contracts satisfied). The two Web cells on dsh 0.1.5-rc.1 were 'surface-incompatible' for a harness-side reason, not a plugin defect: the DSH 0.1.5-rc.1 Web profile itself aborted at boot in @deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot@0.1.5-rc.3 with 'dsh: user patch-layer watching requires the Cordis HMR service', before any HTTP surface existed; the plugin's own registration stage passed in both, and the failure is byte-identical across Node 22 and Node 24. This matches the plugin's own release.yml note that the 0.1.5-rc 'latest' line is transitively broken on npm. No SDK, ACP, headless, or TUI plane was evidenced or scheduled, so no adapter cells ran. No live handles remained at inspect time, so no cancellation was required.
